Subject: QBR prep: slot allocation, burst pool & unit-econ inputs

Team — kicking off a concise QBR thread focused on the infra capacity and unit-economics slice. Goal: give Execs a clean set of tradeoffs and asks (3 slides + appendix) by EOD next Tuesday (2028-12-10). Key inputs I need from each of you below. I attached a short template to align formatting.

Asks (deliverables and numbers):
- Capacity forecast: expected sustained slot utilization and peak burst for next 12 weeks (include 95th pct). — Marissa
- Unit economics scenarios: GPU $/hour, amortized infra overhead, token/unit costs for 3 workload mixes (chat-heavy, embedding-heavy, inference-batch). — Karthik
- OKR check-ins: red/amber/green for infra OKRs tied to runway and capacity automation. Note any significant blockers. — Lauren

Specific knobs we should show in the QBR slide deck:
- Burst pool sizing (recommendation + risk): how much reserved vs. on-demand to hold for 99.9% SLOs
- Batching tradeoffs: expected p50/p95/p99 token latency at three batching profiles (agg batch sizes of 1, 8, 32)
- KV/prefix cache effect: delta in token cost and p95 latency for 20%/40%/60% hit rates

Please reply inline with the numbers or attach a short sheet. If you have model-run data (p99 latency tail or billing adj), include it.

[Attachment: qbr_prep_template.docx (docx)]

Thanks — D

Subject: Re: QBR prep: slot allocation, burst pool & unit-econ inputs — GPU scenarios + batch analysis

Folks — have sketched three unit-econ scenarios and a simple latency table (raw numbers from internal perf runs). Summary first, then a tiny table:

Scenario summaries:
- Conservative (reserve-heavy): Higher $/token (~+22%) but p99 latency stable; reserved discounts apply. Best for customers needing strict low-tail latencies.
- Balanced (recommended): Mix of reserved + 15% burst; adopt 4-bit quant for larger models where accuracy OK; expect ~8–12% $/token savings vs Conservative.
- Aggressive (cost-first): Maximize on-demand and aggressive batching, ~-18% $/token vs Balanced but p99 tail risk; requires KV cache hit >=45% to be viable.

Batching & latency snapshot (generated from 8k token seq tests):
- Batch size 1: p50 60ms, p95 220ms, p99 380ms
- Batch size 8: p50 72ms, p95 260ms, p99 520ms
- Batch size 32: p50 110ms, p95 420ms, p99 980ms

KV cache impact (empirical): 20% hit -> ~6% token cost reduction, 40% hit -> ~13% reduction, 60% hit -> ~20% reduction (also reduces p95 by ~90–150ms depending on model length).

Risks / tradeoffs to highlight:
- Continuous batching increases average throughput cost-effectively but amplifies p99 latency for small-sized requests. Show p99 tail in appendix.
- Quantization: good for cost but needs per-model QA; call out 8-bit vs 4-bit accuracy delta for our top-5 models.

I attached the CSV with the run-level numbers for the slides. I'll produce two quick charts (cost vs p99 and cache-hit sensitivity) for the appendix.

Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: QBR prep: slot allocation, burst pool & unit-econ inputs — ops forecast

Adding ops forecast and a proposal for slot allocation. Short version: we recommend setting the overprovision index to 1.12 for the next 8 weeks and creating a 15% burst pool (pre-warmed) to cover 99.5% of expected spikes. Rationale: recent traffic patterns show short high-frequency spikes (10–15 min) where autoscale cold starts still contribute ~200ms p95 delta.

Proposed allocation (next quarter):
- Base reserved slots: cover 70% of average sustained demand
- Pre-warmed burst pool: 15% (allocated across regions, callable by routing policy)
- On-demand buffer: 15% (elastic)

Operational notes:
- We'll run a controlled experiment next week to validate that a pre-warmed pool reduces p95 tail by ~120ms for chat-heavy workloads.
- If we see sustained utilization >82% for 3 consecutive days, Ops will automatically recommend increasing reserved capacity and flag finance.

Drive link with the forecast + raw telemetry: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AqZ-slot-burst-qbr-prep

Marissa
Head of Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference
